bridge.label: Horn satisfiability
bridge.evidence: The board target returns a satisfying assignment or NO-SOLUTION for an explicit Horn CNF formula. Every Horn CNF formula is a CNF formula. A solution of graph Satisfiability on the identical formula is therefore a legal board output, and NO-SOLUTION is preserved. The reverse direction is invalid because arbitrary CNF is not Horn.

cases.algorithmic_consequence: If the unverified BFS-tree-support to Horn-SAT rule is correct and has polynomial construction and recovery, the source has a polynomial-time search algorithm because Horn-SAT can produce a witness or certify unsatisfiability in polynomial time.
cases.limitation: The large topology count mostly follows the Horn-SAT to general-SAT inclusion and the graph's broad SAT descendants. It must not be interpreted as 94 independent research breakthroughs.

bridge.label: 2-SAT search
bridge.evidence: The board target returns a satisfying assignment or NO-SOLUTION for explicit 2-CNF. Graph KSatisfiability<K2> is the two-literal search variant. Convert any shorter clauses to equivalent exact-two clauses with fresh variables, then restrict a graph solution to the original variables. An empty clause is handled by a fixed unsatisfiable two-clause instance. This preserves both witness and NO-SOLUTION outputs in one call.

cases.algorithmic_consequence: If the unverified common-stable-matching to 2-SAT-search rule is correct with polynomial construction and recovery, the restricted common-stable-matching source has a polynomial-time search algorithm.
cases.limitation: Most of the 94 new problem-family relations arise because the graph contains many descendants of two-literal SAT. This reachability does not itself measure how consequential solving the restricted stable-matching question would be.
